Title: Diagnosis of test `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStreamTest.survivesBlankLinesInPaxHeader`

Details:
The test `survivesBlankLinesInPaxHeader` reads a tar archive file `/COMPRESS-355.tar` using `TarArchiveInputStream` and expects to read an entry named `"package/package.json"` and then have no further entries.

From the `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry` method, we see that this method reads the next tar entry header to create a `TarArchiveEntry` object. If the entry is a Pax header (`isPaxHeader()`), it calls the `paxHeaders()` method to parse the Pax headers and then proceeds.

Looking at the `paxHeaders` method, it calls `parsePaxHeaders` to read and parse the Pax header entries from the stream. The Pax header format it processes expects lines formatted as `"length keyword=value\n"` and parses those into `Map<String, String>` headers.

In the `parsePaxHeaders` method, the reading logic expects to read the length, then a space, then the keyword=value and newline. If the rest length after the keyword is 1, it is interpreted as just a newline and this keyword entry is removed from the header map.

The bug likely is related to how blank lines are being handled in the Pax header content parsing in `parsePaxHeaders()`. If the header data contains blank lines (extra newlines or lines with just whitespace), this method potentially misinterprets or fails to skip over those cleanly as it is tightly parsing the exact format of length and keyword=value per line. This could cause improper header parsing or throwing of exceptions or premature EOF.

Thus, the failure in test suggests that blank lines in the Pax header of `/COMPRESS-355.tar` are causing `parsePaxHeaders` to malfunction, leading to failure when reading the next tar entry with `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry()`. The method attempting to parse the Pax header data doesn't tolerate blank lines well, which violates expectations in the test.

---

The best method locations to fix would be:
- `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders(java.io.InputStream)`
- `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.paxHeaders()`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
